html:
Württemberg was a state in southwest Germany, ruled from Stuttgart. It was a duchy of the Holy Roman Empire from 1495, a Protestant land of small farms and craft towns, and it is on the map from 1783 to 1815.

Like Bavaria, it grew by siding with Napoleon. Its duke became an elector in 1803 and king in 1806, and its land roughly doubled with church lands and small territories taken over in those years. It joined the Confederation of the Rhine and left it in 1813.

In 1819 King William I agreed a constitution with an elected chamber. Many people emigrated in hard years, to Russia and to America. Württemberg joined the German Empire in 1871 and became a republic in 1918.
